operations.text: 0.3.22 settles who decides what about tests, and it supersedes 0.3.21's required-note rule. One: review.md gains the section The project's test policy and the auditor. The project decides what is tested and at which layer - its test policy is the section Test policy of your overrides document and any document that section names - and every readiness and review brief now names it to the auditor on a TEST POLICY line. The auditor decides whether a test that exists is honest and whether the code is correct; the absence of a test your policy excludes is never a finding. A floor no project policy lowers: a behavior that writes stored data, computes money, or sits on a migration, access-policy, grants, auth or permission-model surface always owes its proof. Two: a weakness in a test over code the Reviewer confirmed is a plain note - listed in the ticket's record, its destination settled at the close, nobody fixes it in the ticket - and a required note, closed by the Writer before the commit with no second pass, only on that floor. Three: the brief's test list is the whole list - a Writer adds no test case its brief does not list and asks instead; a case the COO adds goes into the ticket with the ruling that needs it, before the dispatch. Four: the record skeleton carries one more row - the auditor's blockers by kind, the effort split between test Writers, production Writers and the fact-check of test prose, and the defects that reached the operator after the close. Five: a helper agent whose hand-back is too long for its reply writes it whole under the scratch directory's agents folder and replies with a summary and the path; Gate 1 opens that one folder to a non-writer agent and nothing else inside the project, and the Claude-hosted Reviewer and QA stay refused everywhere. Three clarifications ride along: the brief's E2E line picks the route row, so a UI ticket with E2E: no has no spec, no E2E run and no QA (work.md, section Routes); the handoff E2E is run by the COO or a check agent it dispatches, and a project whose overrides document says so accepts the Writer's kept green run instead (work.md, section Tests); and tripwire 4's instrument made to fail on purpose is a script, a grep or a gate - a test follows review.md, section Test quality. This update re-renders ORCHESTRATOR.md, work.md, ticket.md, plan.md, review.md and the Writer agent, each additions block carried. If your overrides document has no section Test policy, the TEST POLICY line reads none and the auditor judges by review.md alone: write the section if you want your own policy to bind the audit. If your project carries a local rule that points the auditor at its test policy, or one that makes a weak test over confirmed code a blocker or a required fix outside the floor, that rule now duplicates or contradicts review.md: delete or narrow it on the operator's word.
